TESTIMONY BEFORE THE JOINT STANDING COMMITTEE ON AGRICULTURE, CONSERVATION, AND FORESTRY
IN SUPPORT OF LD 2006
Resolve, Authorizing the Director of the Bureau ofParks and Lands to Make Certain Land Transactions in Aroostook and Somerset Counties
January 7, 2026
Senator Ross, Representative Pluecker, and members of the Joint Standing Committee on
Agriculture, Conservation, and Forestry, my name is Andy Cutko, and I am the Director of the
Bureau of Parks and Lands (BPL) within the Department of Agriculture, Conservation and
Forestry (DACF). I am speaking in favor of LD 2006, Resolve, Authorizing the Director of the
Bureau ofParks and Lands to Make Certain Land Transactions in Aroostook and Somerset
Counties.
The resolve would authorize the Bureau of Parks and Lands to convey the State's interest in lots
in three different locations.
- In Westmanland, Aroostook County, the Town has requested that the Bureau convey,
without cost, the State's interest in approximately seven acres of Public Reserved Land to
the Town of Westmanland. The seven acres represent the section of the Little Madawaska
Lake Road that is currently designated as Maine -Public Reserved Lands under the Bureau
of Parks and Lands. The purpose of the conveyance is to enable the Town to improve and maintain this section of road by which several Town property taxpayers access their
property. Bureau staff support this transfer with the conditions, including a reverter
clause as well as Town payment of any transaction costs.

- In Seboomook Township, the resolve authorizes the Bureau of Parks and Lands to sell to
the owners of 51 Sebey Lane in Big W Township, approximately 0.25 acres of Public
Reserved Land. The parcel represents the land containing an existing septic system that serves 51 Sebey Lane, which was installed prior to State ownership of the land. Due to the small size and modest value, the Director of the Btueau of Parks and Lands would negotiate a price for the land or, if needed, obtain an appraisal that shall be paid for by the buyer. The buyer will pay all transaction costs, including survey, legal, and recording
costs for the transaction.

- In Presque Isle, Aroostook County, the Resolve authorizes the Director of the Bureau of Parks and Lands to engage in a minor land exchange of less than 0.25 acre with Towers North, Inc. The land swap will rectify a recently identified boundary issue in which a communication tower occupies a very small portion of state land. Towers North Inc. will pay all transaction costs, including legal and recording costs for the transaction. Because this transaction will be an exchange rather than a conveyance, it will not constitute a reduction in state ownership and therefore does not require legislative
approval. However, we have included it here for general awareness.
I would be happy to answer any questions now or at the work session.

LD 2006, "Resolve, Authorizing the Director of the Bureau of Parks and Lands to Make Certain
Land Transactions in Aroostook and Somerset Counties" Joint Standing Committee on Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry
Public Hearing January 7, 2026
1:00pm
Senator Talbot Ross, Representative Pluecker and Esteemed Members of the Joint Standing Committee on
Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry:
I am Senator Sue Bernard and I represent District 1, comprised of 37 communities in Northern Aroostook
County. I am here today to present LD 2006, "Resolve, Authorizing the Director of the Bureau of Parks and
Lands to Make Certain Land Transactions in Aroostook and Somerset Counties."
Citizens of Westmanland reached out to me regarding the next steps in allowing the town to purchase a road
from the State of Maine. The town had been in communication with the Bureau of Parks and Lands about the purchase of the Little Madawaska Lake Road.
One of the requirements for this transaction was that the town vote to purchase this land from the State of Maine. During the town meeting in March of 2025 this was approved, and a letter was sent to the Bureau of
Parks and Lands.
One of my constituents informed me this is an important transaction for those who live on the road. As it
stands now, the town cannot receive any grant money for maintenance of the Little Madawaska Lake Road and the State does not have an interest in maintaining the road. The road runs to the lots on the lake which were sold in the 1990s. The road is a dead end, and the fire lanes are no longer useable. Because this is considered state land, the town does not have an obligation to maintain the road. There are approximately 30 full-time residents now and the subject has been brought up numerous times regarding whether the town may even have a liability for doing maintenance on that portion of road.
If the town acquires the road as this bill directs, then the confusion on who is responsible for the
maintenance of the road will be eliminated; and grant monies received by the town can be used for this road
maintenance.
This bill also authorizes land transactions outside of my district. There are others who will speak after me
on the importance of these transactions.
Each one of these land transactions alleviate confusing land ownership disagreements and benefits both parties involved. For these reasons, I urge you to vote Ought to Pass.
Thank you for your time. I am happy to answer questions, but I encourage you to direct them to those who follow me as they have more firsthand knowledge.
